newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia given extra Brazil car export quota.
newsitem.headline: Kia given extra Brazil car export quota.

text.p: The trade ministry said on Friday Kia Motors Corp had been allowed to export an additional 3,200 cars and vans to Brazil by August 20 under the country's tariff quota system.
The amount is part of the 16,550 units allocated to South Korea for the year to August 20, a ministry statement said.
Brazil had been offering a 50 percent tariff cut to vehicle imports under the quota system.
Kia will be able to export the additional units using part of another automaker's quota. Kia's original quota figure was not immediately available.
Kia was the only South Korean auto maker that had already filled up its individual quota and would otherwise have had to export vehicles without tariff favours, the official said.

Kia Motors, one of South Korea's top three auto makers, has been struggling under its parent group's financial troubles, widely attributed to sagging domestic car sales and poor performance by its affiliates.
On Tuesday, the nation's eighth-largest Kia Group was offered protection by its creditor banks.
